reason: Array Labs is a $20M-Series-A, ~36-person radar/geospatial company selling sensing to DoD and IC customers, and its live Capture and Proposal Manager req confesses it has no government-transition machinery at all — "You will not inherit a large capture organization; you will help build the operating system for how Array pursues and wins government work" — the exact prototype-to-program gap Barry Hess fixes.

company.name: Array Labs, Inc.
company.one_liner: Builds and operates clusters of small SAR (radar) satellites that image the same area from multiple angles simultaneously to produce high-resolution 3D geospatial data for government and commercial customers.
company.industry: Aerospace / defense / space-based radar and geospatial intelligence
company.stage: Series A — $20M led by Catapult Ventures announced 2026-01-05; $35M total raised since Y Combinator (S22); ~36-39 employees

evidence_jobs.quote: You will not inherit a large capture organization; you will help build the operating system for how Array pursues and wins government work, from pursuit plans and proposal rhythms to compliance discipline, technical storytelling, and award handoffs.

evidence_jobs.title: Capture and Proposal Manager, Government (supporting line, same live posting)
evidence_jobs.quote: As government customers seek faster and more cost-effective ways to field advanced capabilities, Array is focused on transitioning new technology into funded programs, prototype efforts, and operational deployments.

talk_track: I ran engineering at a DoD small business for 16 years and fielded a patented tactical mapping platform that operators used in theater. It still died force-wide, because nobody senior inside the building carried it. Your Capture and Proposal Manager req says the hire "will not inherit a large capture organization" and will "build the operating system for how Array pursues and wins government work." The non-obvious read: capture wins the award, but what turns a prototype award into a program of record is an advocacy chain — an operator who needs it, a program manager who budgets it, and a technical story that survives their evaluation, not yours. That work is technical and much of it happens inside a SCIF, which is why the clearance line on that req sitting under "preferred" is the part I would price first. Worth mapping before your next program office evaluation?
notes: Liveness re-verified 2026-07-23 by Exa livecrawl of the Lever posting (crawl status: success). Other live Array Labs reqs today: Radar Signal Processing Engineer (MTI/STAP), Space Systems Engineer, Engineering Program Manager, Technical Program Manager, Senior Commercial Counsel — those are ordinary engineering scaling hires and are NOT the signal. Caveats: headcount ~36-39 sits just above Barry's stated 8-30 ICP band, and the founding team is technically deep (CEO Andrew Peterson, ex-General Atomics radar / Moog), so the gap is specifically cleared, government-facing technical leadership rather than engineering competence. No CTO is publicly listed; public exec record shows Andrew Peterson (Co-Founder & CEO) and Isaac Robledo (Founder, Strategy & GTM).
